text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cabinet considers merging pension and social security laws in face of rapid rise in pension costs, sources say.
- Consumer association calls for government cuts in food prices after fall in world prices for chick-peas. But restaurants call for price rises to balance their 10 percent sales tax.
- Russian Foreign Minister Primakov, leaving Jordan at the end of a Middle East tour, praises King Hussein's stance and calls for resumption of multilateral Arab-Israeli talks.
- Trainee lawyers to protest today over exam results.
- Prime Minister Kabariti heads meeting of higher council for privatisation. Says economic reform must continue with clarity and transparency.
- King Hussein meets Maronite bishops from Jordan and the holy lands.
- Israeli President Ezer Weizman to make his first visit to Jordan on Wednesday.
